editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit the compiled path before trusting an agent-workflow check
dailyInsight.insight: Pydantic AI’s fresh workflow-policy guard supports one bounded audit for teams that run coding agents in GitHub Actions: inspect the generated workflow graph for conditions that read undeclared dependencies, and confirm that the compiled file—not just the editable prompt source—changes with the intended policy. The project’s source-level change encodes historical cases where an agentic workflow could skip while the required check still appeared successful.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The guard parses the workflow that Actions actually runs and rejects `needs.<job>` expressions that do not name declared dependencies, source changes without a regenerated lock, unreachable agent prompt paths, mismatched timeout budgets, and other configuration shapes that can turn intended agent work into a silent no-op. The focused regression suite reconstructs the broken dependency graph and expects an actionable violation.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A prompt can be sound while the compiled configuration never schedules the agent, gives it an unusable workspace path, or runs an older lock. Checking the execution path is a reversible way to distinguish a passing status from evidence that the intended agent job was reachable.

actions.audience: Maintainer or platform engineer operating coding-agent workflows in GitHub Actions
actions.label: Trace one agent check from source to compiled graph
actions.instruction: In a disposable branch or checkout, choose one agent workflow and compare its human-edited source with the generated workflow that Actions executes. For every `needs.<job>` used in a condition or interpolation, confirm that job is declared as a dependency; then make a harmless source-only change and verify the required generated artifact changes with it. Do not use production credentials or trigger destructive agent tools for this audit.

receipts.title: Guard agentic workflows against silent waste, and report gh-aw spend weekly to Slack (#6853)
receipts.supports: Shows the fresh source change that adds the workflow-policy guard, CI wiring, and regression tests for documented silent agent-workflow failure modes.

receipts.title: Pydantic AI workflow guidance for gh-aw agentic workflows
receipts.supports: Explains that the editable Markdown workflows compile into generated lock files and that GitHub Actions runs the generated locks, which is why the compiled path is the audit target.

confidence.basis: A fresh public commit, its guard implementation and reconstructed regression tests, and the project’s workflow guide agree on the source-versus-compiled execution boundary.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are source-level receipts from Pydantic AI. They do not establish that a particular hosted workflow, release, or agent run completed, nor do they prove that another agent platform has the same compilation and skipping behavior.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public GitHub Actions semantics show that an undeclared `needs` reference fails loudly rather than resolving empty in the covered positions, if the generated lock is not the artifact Action executes, or if Pydantic AI removes the guard in favor of a demonstrably equivalent check.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for end-to-end workflow fixtures that prove a real agent job starts, receives the intended context, and emits a bounded result after the static guard passes.
